items.headline: Nebius and Nvidia launch open-source 'Physical AI Workbench' for robotics teams
items.summary: Cloud provider Nebius, working with Nvidia, released an open-source toolkit that bundles data generation, simulation (Cosmos, Isaac Sim, Isaac GR00T) and training/evaluation into one agent-driven workflow, aiming to cut the glue-code robotics teams need to build physical AI systems.

items.headline: AI-assisted audit uncovers critical PHP flaws, prompting emergency patches across the web
items.summary: A security audit aided by an OpenAI model and researchers at Wiz uncovered two critical memory-safety bugs (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) affecting most PHP-powered websites; PHP shipped emergency patches for the 8.5, 8.4, 8.3 and 8.2 branches on October 21, and attackers began probing within days.

items.headline: Node.js patches critical Brotli decoder flaw allowing remote code execution
items.summary: Node.js's October 2026 security release fixed ten vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-111497, a CVSS 9.2 out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decompression library that could let attackers execute arbitrary code; users are urged to upgrade to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1.

items.headline: AI lab Recursive releases Flint, an open-weight coding model built largely by its own AI research system
items.summary: Richard Socher's startup Recursive launched Flint, a free, laptop-runnable coding model it says was built in under four months with heavy help from its automated 'Eureka Machine' research system, an early example of AI meaningfully accelerating its own model development.

items.headline: Replit's CEO says the company has dropped Anthropic's Claude as its default coding model for OpenAI
items.summary: At a public event, Replit CEO Amjad Masad said the company is no longer working with Anthropic and now defaults to OpenAI's models, citing cost among the reasons, though a source close to the deal disputed that the partnership has fully ended.

items.headline: Anthropic pitches Congress a confidential frontier AI safety bill with a 50-death threshold
items.summary: Politico reported that Anthropic circulated draft federal legislation that would let regulators block an AI model's release only if it poses a foreseeable risk of over $1 billion in damage or more than 50 deaths from bio-weapons, rogue agentic behavior or cyberattacks, drawing criticism that the bar is set too high.

items.headline: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon teaches a humanoid robot to play cornhole from a single video
items.summary: DeepMind said its Gemini 4 Argon model watched one video of a person throwing cornhole bags, built its own physics simulation to practice in, then transferred that skill to Apptronik's Apollo humanoid, which sank seven throws in a row in a real-world test.

items.headline: Fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were pushed out for raising concerns; company denies it
items.summary: Three former OpenAI safety staffers, Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, told NPR they believe they were dismissed in retaliation for safety advocacy and contact with outside researchers; OpenAI says they were fired for separate breaches of trust unrelated to safety speech.

items.headline: ABB expands OmniCore EyeMotion with an 'AI Robot Trainer' for vision-guided manufacturing
items.summary: At China's CIIF 2026 trade fair, ABB Robotics unveiled an AI Robot Trainer that pairs with its OmniCore EyeMotion vision platform to let non-specialists set up AI-guided pick-and-place, bin-picking and inspection tasks, claiming up to 90% faster commissioning alongside two new compact industrial robots.
